issues.evidence: The existing CSV public route now dispatches internally to a distinct whitespace-row grammar when RFC delimiters/quotes are absent.
Incidence parsing tracks first explicit time/weight values and their rows; a later different explicit value rejects the whole parse.
H2H uses a bounded cursor parser with full RHS consumption; adjacency requires exactly one structural colon and at least one neighbor.
Detection examines the complete relevant document structure and routes once; it does not parse every format until one succeeds.
RFC-decoded row/incidence identifiers and time payload survive both the format parser and the shared canonical commit boundary. Default raw-text cleanup remains unchanged.
H2H no longer strips/reinserts h prefixes and preserves supported arbitrary exporter IDs, including reserved names, spaces, commas, and literal quote characters.

compatibilityDecisions.decision: Keep the existing csv route; select a separately testable whitespace-row or RFC CSV lexer internally.
Select edgelist when every relevant row has exactly two tokens because its canonical pair-hyperedge output is equivalent; mixed widths select csv/whitespace rows.
Auto-detect only the strong multi-row signature of a repeated hyperedge-like first column; otherwise preserve normal CSV precedence and allow explicit Incidence selection.
A line such as h1: garbage remains Simple by existing structural precedence because it is valid H2V text; an H2H shared-clause or (none) marker routes to strict H2H validation.
Reject A: because the canonical hypergraph produced by this adapter represents undirected pairs and has no standalone-vertex representation.

knownFormatLimitations.detail: H2H carries shared memberships only; exclusive vertices, graph metadata, and shared-vertex tokens containing the unescaped H2H separators cannot be reconstructed.
